title: Physiology / Anatomy and Physiology
description: Physiology / Anatomy and Physiology studies the human body as an integrated structure-function system. Students move from anatomical language, cells, tissues, and homeostasis into organ systems, regulatory physiology, laboratory identification, physiological measurement, clinical mechanisms, and integrative case reasoning.

topics.title: Anatomical Language, Body Organization, Tissues, and Homeostasis
topics.description: Students learn the structural map of the body and the regulatory logic that keeps internal conditions stable.

children.title: Anatomical orientation
children.description: The point is to describe structures precisely so communication is unambiguous.

children.title: Levels of organization
children.description: Students see how cells, tissues, organs, and systems build function at increasing scale.

children.title: Homeostatic regulation
children.description: Homeostasis explains how the body senses change and restores controlled variables.

topics.title: Cell Physiology, Membranes, Transport, and Signaling
topics.description: This module builds the cellular mechanisms that explain organ-system function.

children.title: Membrane structure and transport
children.description: Cell membranes control exchange and create gradients that power physiology.

children.title: Cell signaling
children.description: Cells coordinate function through chemical messengers and receptor pathways.

children.title: Cellular energy and adaptation
children.description: Physiological work depends on ATP production and adaptive cellular responses.

topics.title: Integumentary, Skeletal, and Joint Systems
topics.description: Students connect protective, structural, mineral-storage, and movement-support functions to anatomy.

children.title: Integumentary system
children.description: Skin protects the body while helping regulate temperature, sensation, and fluid balance.

children.title: Skeletal system
children.description: Bones provide support, leverage, mineral storage, and blood-cell formation.

children.title: Joints and movement support
children.description: Joint structure determines motion, stability, and injury risk.

topics.title: Muscular System and Movement Physiology
topics.description: This topic explains how muscle structure, excitation, contraction, and metabolism produce movement and force.

children.title: Muscle anatomy
children.description: Muscle organization links gross anatomy to microscopic force production.

children.title: Excitation-contraction coupling
children.description: Electrical signals become mechanical force through calcium-controlled cross-bridge cycling.

children.title: Muscle energetics and performance
children.description: Muscle function changes with fuel, fatigue, training, and fiber type.

topics.title: Nervous System, Neurophysiology, and Sensory Systems
topics.description: Students learn how electrical signaling, synapses, neural circuits, and sensory pathways coordinate the body.

children.title: Neurons and action potentials
children.description: Electrical excitability is the language of rapid control.

children.title: Synapses and neural circuits
children.description: Neurons communicate through chemical and electrical synapses to form functional pathways.

children.title: Sensory and autonomic systems
children.description: Sensory input and autonomic output connect the body to internal and external conditions.

topics.title: Endocrine System and Hormonal Regulation
topics.description: This module develops hormonal signaling as a slower but powerful system for coordinated regulation.

children.title: Hormone classes and receptors
children.description: Hormone chemistry determines how signals travel and how cells respond.

children.title: Major endocrine axes
children.description: Endocrine glands coordinate growth, metabolism, stress, reproduction, and calcium balance.

children.title: Endocrine integration
children.description: Hormones rarely act alone, so students learn coordinated regulation across systems.

topics.title: Cardiovascular System, Blood, and Hemodynamics
topics.description: Students study the heart, vessels, blood, pressure, flow, and transport functions that support every tissue.

children.title: Heart anatomy and electrophysiology
children.description: Cardiac structure and conduction explain pumping rhythm and coordinated contraction.

children.title: Blood and vessels
children.description: Blood composition and vessel structure support transport, pressure, and exchange.

children.title: Hemodynamics
children.description: Students learn how pressure, resistance, flow, and cardiac output are regulated.

topics.title: Lymphatic System, Immunity, and Host Defense
topics.description: This topic covers fluid return, immune surveillance, inflammation, and adaptive protection.

children.title: Lymphatic anatomy
children.description: The lymphatic system returns fluid and provides routes for immune surveillance.

children.title: Innate immunity
children.description: Innate defenses respond quickly to injury, infection, and foreign material.

children.title: Adaptive immunity
children.description: Adaptive immunity provides specificity, memory, and targeted defense.

topics.title: Respiratory System and Gas Exchange
topics.description: Students learn how ventilation, diffusion, perfusion, and control of breathing sustain oxygen and carbon dioxide balance.

children.title: Respiratory anatomy and ventilation
children.description: Airway and lung structure determine how air reaches exchange surfaces.

children.title: Gas exchange and transport
children.description: Oxygen and carbon dioxide movement depends on diffusion, perfusion, and blood chemistry.

children.title: Control of breathing
children.description: Respiratory control maintains blood gases and acid-base status.

topics.title: Renal System, Fluid-Electrolyte Balance, and Acid-Base Physiology
topics.description: This module explains kidney function, body-fluid regulation, electrolyte control, and pH homeostasis.

children.title: Nephron structure and filtration
children.description: Kidney function begins with selective filtration and nephron specialization.

children.title: Reabsorption and secretion
children.description: The kidney fine-tunes body fluids by moving solutes and water along the nephron.

children.title: Hormonal control by ADH and aldosterone
Acid-base balance
children.description: Renal and respiratory systems cooperate to regulate pH.

topics.title: Digestive System, Metabolism, and Nutrition Physiology
topics.description: Students connect gastrointestinal anatomy with digestion, absorption, liver function, metabolism, and energy balance.

children.title: Gastrointestinal anatomy and motility
children.description: Structure and coordinated movement prepare food for digestion and absorption.

children.title: Digestion and absorption
children.description: Students learn how macromolecules become usable nutrients.

children.title: Metabolism and liver function
children.description: The GI system integrates with liver, pancreas, and metabolism to regulate energy balance.

topics.title: Reproductive System, Development, and Life-Span Physiology
topics.description: This topic covers reproductive anatomy, endocrine cycles, development, pregnancy physiology, and aging.

children.title: Reproductive anatomy and gametogenesis
children.description: Structure supports gamete production, fertilization, and reproductive function.

children.title: Hormonal cycles and pregnancy
children.description: Reproductive physiology is coordinated through endocrine rhythms and developmental support.

children.title: Life-span physiology
children.description: Physiological function changes across development, adulthood, and aging.

topics.title: Integrative Physiology, Exercise, Stress, and Environmental Adaptation
topics.description: Students learn how multiple systems coordinate responses to exercise, stress, temperature, altitude, and changing environments.

children.title: Exercise integration
children.description: Exercise reveals how cardiovascular, respiratory, muscular, neural, and endocrine systems work together.

children.title: Stress physiology
children.description: Stress responses coordinate neural, endocrine, immune, and metabolic changes.

children.title: Environmental physiology
children.description: The body adapts to external challenges through integrated regulation.

topics.title: Pathophysiology Bridges and Clinical Case Reasoning
topics.description: This module uses disease mechanisms to test whether students truly understand normal physiology.

children.title: Homeostasis failure
children.description: Disease often begins when feedback systems can no longer maintain regulated variables.

children.title: System-specific cases
children.description: Cases help students test anatomy and physiology knowledge in realistic contexts.

children.title: Clinical reasoning basics
children.description: Students learn to explain symptoms and data from mechanisms rather than memorizing labels.

topics.title: Anatomy and Physiology Laboratory, Data, and Integrative Project
topics.description: The course culminates in identification, physiological measurement, data analysis, and a polished integrative case or research project.

children.title: Anatomy identification
children.description: Lab work turns names and diagrams into spatial understanding.

children.title: Physiology measurements
children.description: Students learn to collect and interpret body-system data.

children.title: Integrative project
children.description: The capstone asks students to connect structure, function, data, and case reasoning.
